prompt_diff_summary: Kept v1's two instruction blocks (current-time grounding, and search-before-giving-up on durations) verbatim, and added three new instruction blocks: (1) balances are always readable from get_user_details and multi-card sums must be stated by the agent itself, (2) get_reservation_details must be called on every reservation id from get_user_details before concluding anything spans multiple reservations, (3) follow the user's explicit payment-split instructions exactly and execute the confirmed action on the very next turn instead of asking for confirmation twice; also appended one sentence to the date-grounding block telling the agent to fold a matched-record finding and its policy consequence into a single message instead of spending an extra turn only confirming which record it found, to avoid the turn-budget regression that broke task 19 in v1.
helper_diff_summary: Unchanged from v1: extra_context(policy) extracts the policy's 'The current time is ...' sentence via regex and re-appends it as a reminder block at the end of the system prompt.
risks: Task 19 regressed in v1 because an extra confirmation turn ('is this the correct reservation?') pushed the final cancel_reservation call past the point where the simulated user said ###STOP###. The new sentence added to the date-grounding block explicitly tells the agent to fold the matched-record statement and policy consequence into one message instead of asking a separate confirmation question, which should restore v0's single-message pattern for that task; risk remains if the model still asks an extra question for other reasons.

The new 'call get_reservation_details on every reservation id' rule could add tool calls (and turns) to tasks that only need one reservation, potentially slowing down simple single-reservation flows; the instruction is scoped to only trigger when the request could span multiple reservations or the matching reservation is not yet certain, to limit this to the cases that actually need it.

The new balances/summed-totals rule and payment-instructions rule are generic and do not reference any task's specific numbers, so they should generalize to the held-out test split's different customers without overfitting.

changes.what: Reused v1's current-time grounding block verbatim, and appended one new sentence instructing the agent to state a matched record and its policy consequence in the same message instead of spending an extra turn only confirming which record it found.
changes.why: This block already fixed tasks 11/22/24 in cycle 1; the appended sentence targets the exact turn-budget mechanism that made this same addition break task 19 (extra 'is this the correct reservation?' turn pushed the cancel_reservation call past the user's ###STOP###).

changes.anchor: CRITICAL — DO NOT GIVE UP TOO EARLY:
changes.what: Reused v1's instruction verbatim requiring the agent to retrieve schedule/duration data with search tools and calculate instead of claiming it is unavailable.
changes.why: This exact block already fixed task 44 in cycle 1 (agent had said duration info was unavailable and offered to transfer).

changes.anchor: CRITICAL — PAYMENT METHOD BALANCES ARE ALREADY AVAILABLE TO YOU:
changes.what: New block stating get_user_details' payment_methods already contains every balance, forbidding claims that balances are unavailable, and requiring the agent itself to state summed totals for multiple gift cards/certificates.
changes.why: Task 14 transcript: agent said 'I don't have the ability to check balances... you may need to contact your bank' despite get_user_details later returning exactly those balances; tasks 14 and 23 both failed COMMUNICATE checks because the user, not the agent, stated the required $327/$1000 sums.

changes.anchor: CRITICAL — CHECK EVERY RESERVATION BEFORE YOU CONCLUDE:
changes.what: New block requiring get_reservation_details to be called on every reservation id returned by get_user_details before deciding anything, whenever the request could span multiple reservations or the matching one isn't yet certain.
changes.why: Task 39 transcript: agent fetched only reservation 8C8K4E out of 7 reservations, wrongly concluded it was already flown, and transferred, never reaching the 6 other reservations the gold trace checks (including the 2 it should have cancelled).

changes.anchor: CRITICAL — FOLLOW THE USER'S PAYMENT INSTRUCTIONS EXACTLY:
changes.what: New block requiring the agent to follow user-specified payment-split rules (order of methods, thresholds, one-certificate-per-reservation) exactly using the calculate tool, and to execute a confirmed action on the very next turn instead of asking for confirmation a second time.
changes.why: Task 25 required an unusual certificate-vs-gift-card threshold rule stated only by the user; task 23 required a per-passenger certificate split across three separate bookings. Neither rule is safe to hard-code since the test split has different customers, so the fix is a generic 'follow the user's explicit payment instructions' rule.

changes.what: Kept v1's extra_context hook unchanged, which re-appends the policy's exact current-time sentence as a reminder at the end of the system prompt.
changes.why: This hook was already present in the held v1 challenger and did not contribute to v1's one regression (task 19, traced to system.md's added confirmation turn, not to this reminder); no reason to change it.
